messages:
perf-bot: nightly perf alert — 2025-10-12 02:12 UTC :warning: 95p latency +28% for /generate-small-batch (small-batch workloads). metric: p95_ms. snapshot: https://dash.redwood/nightly/alerts/1751234567

alex: saw the alert. which change could have hit kernel selection? affected: release branch, route /generate-small-batch.

ci-bot: perf-check: PR #4321 (merged) — small-batch throughput -12%, p95 +25% on our micro-batch harness. full run: https://ci.redwood/pipeline/4321/perf-check

maria: that was my merge earlier today (01:07 UTC) — PR 4321: kernel-selector now prefers `fused_matmul` on nvptx when `seq_len <= 64`. I thought fused path was strictly faster.

alex: hmm. alert matches seq_len<=64 micro-batches. can someone repro locally quickly?

lucy: repro done on my dev rig (A100). config: batch=4, seq=8, model=xl-7b. baseline (before merge) vs current: p95 42ms -> 55ms. nvprof shows many more kernel launches and worse occupancy on fused path.

lucy: ```
# quick perf summary
baseline p95: 42ms
after PR4321 p95: 55ms
nvprof snippet: kernel 'matmul_fused' launch_count=324 (avg 0.17ms) vs previous matmul launch_count=98 (avg 0.12ms)
```

maria: thanks lucy. my change picks fused when estimated GEMM shape fits small-window heuristic. looks like per-request padding and per-request variance cause fragmentation, leading to smaller work per kernel and higher overhead.

tj: can we bisect the release to confirm PR4321 is the culprit? I'll start a git bisect on release-2025-10 and run the micro-batch perf harness.

tj: update: bisect narrowed to commit 3e9f7b2 (PR4321 merge commit). reproducible locally.

alex: OK. plan: revert on release branch, hold canary, then follow with a targeted fix that gates fused_matmul for micro-batches / low occupancy. who can open revert?

lucy: opened revert PR #4330 (revert 3e9f7b2) at 02:35 UTC and applied to staging canary (3 instances). staging p95 returned to 43ms. smoke link: https://ci.redwood/4330/smoke

maria: rolling back now. I'll also push a follow-up patch that adds an occupancy threshold check and ties the selector to `estimated_flops_per_launch`. will add unit tests and a perf harness regression test for seq<=64, batch<=8.

sre: I'll hold the release rollout and mute noisy alerts for the route for 24h while we verify. filed rollout hold: ROLL-1921.

perf-bot: noted — muting nightly alerts for /generate-small-batch for 24h and creating a post-check job to re-evaluate tomorrow.

alex: good triage. action items: (1) maria to open fix PR and perf tests, (2) lucy to add micro-batch regression to CI, (3) tj verify staging canary across variety of GPUs, (4) sre hold rollout. please add quick notes to the perf postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

maria: will follow up with PR and tests in next 2 hours.

lucy: i'll add the harness case and a short note in docs/perf/triage/1751234567.md.

alex: thanks everyone — we'll re-run nightly and confirm next run.
